before:
Ainu's classification as a language isolate, surveyed in
		<Xr ch="genetic-position-macro-comparison" />, means that no genetic relationship accounts
		for resemblances between Ainu and Japanese vocabulary. Demonstrable shared items are contact
		loans, and the directionality of that contact is asymmetric by period and domain.
after:
No genetic relationship between Ainu and Japanese has been established
		(<Xr ch="genetic-position-macro-comparison" />). Proposed loans require evidence for
		contact and borrowing direction; lexical resemblance alone does not establish either
		<Ref k="vovin2022" p="185–188" />.
evidence: Isolate classification denotes no demonstrated relationship; Vovin 2022 pp185–188 argues individual etymologies using specific comparative evidence.

before: found'. The compound ni-kap-us-i — ni 'tree' + kap 'bark' + -us-i 'habitually-at' — yields 'place where bark trees stand', commonly cited as the source of Niikappu 新冠 (illustrative only; ). The suffix also surfaces in Usu 有珠 and several other Hokkaido names.
after: found' . Niikappu 新冠 is recorded as nikap 'tree bark' in the town's historical account ; its components are ni 'tree' and kap 'bark' .
evidence: Niikappu town newsletter 2024-11 no694 p7, 新冠百話 第七十三話: ニカプ 木の皮 / ニレの皮; no habitual/nominalizing sequence.
